description: A collection of modern/faster/saner alternatives to common unix commands.

summary.one_liner: A curated list of modern, faster, and more user-friendly replacements for classic Unix command-line tools like cat, ls, find, grep, ps, and top.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a list of command-line tools, each with a one-line description of what it replaces or improves on. It covers file viewing (bat as a cat clone with syntax highlighting), file listing (eza, lsd as ls alternatives), diffs and git output (delta), disk usage and free space (dust, duf), directory navigation (broot, zoxide), and searching (fd for find, ripgrep for grep, fzf for fuzzy finding, mcfly for shell history). It also lists text processing tools (choose for cut/awk, jq for JSON, sd for sed), cheatsheet and man page helpers (cheat, tldr), system and process monitors (bottom, glances, gtop, procs for ps), benchmarking and ping (hyperfine, gping), HTTP clients (httpie, curlie, xh), DNS (doggo), and git UI (lazygit). Entries are a flat list with no install commands or grouping headers. The sd entry includes two example shell invocations.
use_cases: find a modern replacement for ls, cat, or grep
pick command-line tools for searching files faster
monitor processes and system resources in the terminal
send HTTP requests from the command line
benchmark commands or graph ping latency
navigate directories and shell history more quickly
notable: Covers over 25 classic Unix commands with a named modern alternative for each
Entries are one-line descriptions with no install instructions
Includes example usage for sd find-and-replace
Spans file, text, process, network, and git tooling in one list
caveats: The README is a bare list with no installation or platform details
Some listed tools are described as Rust-based, but the README does not say which languages each tool uses
No license is stated in the README
